label: Blacktip reef shark (Carcharhinus melanopterus), typical adult, side view

image.author: Kakidai (Wikimedia Commons user; Artist field from Commons API)
image.license: CC BY-SA 3.0 (from Commons API extmetadata LicenseShortName)
image.species_shown: Carcharhinus melanopterus (per file title; consistent with the photo: black-tipped first dorsal and caudal fins, pale ventral surface, fusiform reef-shark body)
image.view: Whole animal in lateral side view, head to the left, slightly nose-down, body horizontal; photographed in an aquarium tank against a rocky backdrop
image.image_observations: Whole shark in clean side profile, snout at left and upper caudal lobe at right, so every part is visible in one silhouette. The first dorsal is large with a black tip, the second dorsal is small and sits above the anal fin on the posterior trunk, and the pectoral fin is broad and low on the flank. The heterocercal tail has a large upper lobe with a black tip and a smaller lower lobe, and the body is slender and fusiform with a height-to-length ratio of about 0.26. These proportions set the revised bounding box, fin positions and lengths; the aquarium setting is not relevant to the geometry.

physical_parsing.volume_method: Prolate-ellipsoid approximation of the fusiform body (semi-axes 0.8 m long, 0.12 m deep, 0.15 m wide, about 0.060 m3), reduced about 10 percent for the tapered caudal peduncle and tail, giving about 0.05 m3. Depth is measured from the side-view photo (body about 0.14 of total length, giving about 0.23 m). Width is not visible in a side view and is kept from the first pass. Estimate only, not a mesh volume.
physical_parsing.shape_class: fusiform (torpedo-shaped) elasmobranch body, dorsoventrally flattened at the snout, laterally compressed at the tail

core.description: Single fusiform core from snout tip (z=+0.5) to caudal peduncle (z about -0.3), centred near (x=0, y=0.40, z=0). The core is about 0.24 m deep at the pectoral region, judged from the photo, and tapers to a narrow peduncle. The caudal fin is a separate structure attached at the posterior end of the core. Head and trunk form one mass with no separate neck.
core.cross_section: rounded-elliptical, flattened ventrally, about 0.24 m deep by 0.3 m wide at the trunk (width not visible in side view), tapering to a compressed (roughly 0.1 m) peduncle

physical_parsing.size_source: Compagno, L.J.V. (1984) FAO Species Catalogue Vol. 4, Sharks of the World, part 2, Carcharhinus melanopterus: maximum about 1.8 m total length, typical adults about 1.5-1.6 m. Stated from memory and not verified against the live source in this session. Also FishBase (Carcharhinus melanopterus) entry.

parts.name: Pectoral fin (left)

penetration.overlap_region: anterior-lateral trunk core behind the gill region, at the pectoral girdle

parts.notes: Large, broad-based, wing-like, mainly for lift and steering. Photo shows the fin low on the flank behind the gill region, with a tip reaching about 0.13 of total length. Hint is a loose match: fin_dorsal is the closest fin shape in the library.

parts.name: Pelvic fin (left)

penetration.overlap_region: ventral-lateral trunk core, pelvic girdle region

parts.notes: Smaller ventral fin, used for stability and pitch control. Photo places the pelvic root at about 0.55 of total length from the snout, as the first pass estimated. Hint is a loose match only.

parts.name: First dorsal fin

penetration.overlap_region: dorsal midline of the trunk core, above the pectoral region

parts.notes: Large, with a black tip in blacktip reef sharks (confirmed in the photo). Provides stability and roll control. Its tip reaches y=1.0 in the normalized frame, so it sets the top of the bounding box. Root is over the pectoral region, slightly forward of centre.

parts.name: Second dorsal fin

penetration.overlap_region: dorsal caudal-trunk core, posterior to the first dorsal

parts.notes: Small, placed over the anal fin on the posterior trunk (confirmed in the photo), and it helps with stability.

parts.name: Anal fin

penetration.overlap_region: ventral caudal-trunk core, posterior to the pelvic fins

parts.notes: Ventral counterpart of the second dorsal fin, sitting slightly anterior to the caudal peduncle. The hint is a shape match only, since fin_dorsal is not ventral by design.

parts.name: Heterocercal caudal (tail) fin

penetration.overlap_region: caudal peduncle end of the core

parts.notes: Heterocercal, meaning the upper lobe is larger than the lower (confirmed in the photo), so the tail produces lift and thrust together. The upper lobe is the main thrust surface, and both lobes have black tips. Main drive for swimming, and flexed laterally about the peduncle.

parts.name: Eye (left)
parts.notes: Dorsolateral placement on the head with a nictitating membrane. Small and mostly stationary. The hint is a rough match.

parts.name: Nostril / nasal capsule (left)
parts.notes: Ventral nostril, a non-protruding inhalant opening for olfaction. No library equivalent. Symmetric pair on the ventral snout.

parts.name: Ampullae of Lorenzini field (left)

penetration.overlap_region: ventral head surface, subdermal canal network

parts.notes: Electroreceptive jelly-filled canals opening through pores on the ventral snout and head. Flush with the skin, so it needs only a shallow surface overlap. No library equivalent.

parts.name: Lateral line canal (left)

penetration.overlap_region: lateral trunk surface along the full body length

parts.notes: Mechanosensory canal along each flank, running from head to tail. Sensitive to water movement. Flush with the skin, so it is a surface detail. No library equivalent.

parts.name: Upper jaw (maxilla / palatoquadrate)

joints.name: jaw suspension to neurocranium (fixed for practical purposes)

parts.notes: Upper jaw carries the upper tooth rows and is largely fixed to the skull. Sharks have no true jaw protrusion here, unlike bony fishes. Hint is a rough match.

parts.name: Lower jaw (mandible)
parts.notes: Opens by rotating down about the mandibular articulation. Carries the lower tooth rows, which are replaced continuously in series.

parts.name: Gill slits, five per side (left)

penetration.overlap_region: lateral branchial region of the head and trunk core

parts.notes: Five slits per side for respiratory water outflow. In the photo the slit row spans about 0.05-0.06 m, so length_m is revised. Not used for prey capture, so the feeding category is the closest fit in this taxonomy. Count is per side.

parts.name: Pelvic clasper (left, males only)
parts.notes: Male-only reproductive grasping organ, a modified inner edge of the pelvic fin. It grasps during mating and is the only manipulation structure. Hint is a poor match, so this is a low-confidence category assignment. Females lack it.

constraints.symmetry: bilateral about the sagittal (X=0) plane, with the caudal fin on the midline. Parts are listed by distinct structure; each pair counts once.
constraints.gait: Lateral undulation of the posterior trunk and caudal fin, with pectoral fins used for lift and steering and pelvic fins for pitch. Caudal fin is heterocercal (asymmetric). Blacktip reef sharks are fast and agile, with frequent sharp turns.
other: Dorsal fin tip sets y=1.0 in the normalized frame; y=0 is the ventral keel of the body, not the ground.
Black-tipped fin margins are colouration only, not a separate structure, so they are not parts.
Dermal denticles (placoid scales) are a surface texture, not a mesh part, so they are omitted and listed under library_gaps.
Teeth are dental rows inside the jaws, not a separate mesh; they are listed under library_gaps.
Normalized positions assume x is scaled by 0.35 m, y by 0.45 m and z by 1.6 m.

library_gaps.why: Flush-to-skin pore fields with no library equivalent; needs a small surface decal or flat disc.
Long, thin sensory canal along the flank. No library equivalent for a flush line.
Ventral, non-protruding inhalant openings. The library has nose_button, but it is a protruding feature.
Repeated slits with a respiratory function. No library equivalent, and the taxonomy has no respiration category.
Dental rows inside the jaws, far too fine for a library part. Needs a texture or decal.
Surface texture. Not a mesh part, and the library has no scale-texture category.
tail_fan is symmetric, so an asymmetric shark tail needs a custom shape.
Reproductive grasping organs. hand_claw is a poor match, and the library has no reproductive or clasping part.
